subject: Fit xyplot (lattice package) onto screen automatically

messages.author: 89c04f2e40dabf01
messages.subject: Fit xyplot (lattice package) onto screen automatically
parts:
I have an application where the user dynamically creates some xyplots from the lattice packages conditional on the data. The "rows" in the graphic layout is configurable. With a single panel, and even with just two rows, my plot seems just fine and visually portrays the information in a way the seems easy to digest.

However, when the layout conditions on multiple variables (typically 3 or more), the xyplot is "squished" in the HTML view and cannot be easily viewed. I have created a minimal example below that just shows one simple plot. Ideally, I would like the individual panels of the trellis plot to be larger.

I hope this is helpful context, if not please let me know if more information is needed.

Can anyone suggest the most appropriate method for filling out the space to display the full xyplot in a dynamic way? By "dynamic" I mean that it would automatically adjust to fill the space depending on the number of rows in the xyplot


### ui.r
shinyUI(fluidPage(

  titlePanel("Hello Shiny!"),

  # Sidebar with a slider input for the number of bins
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("bins",
                  "Number of bins:",
                  min = 1,
                  max = 50,
                  value = 30)
    ),

    # Show a plot of the generated distribution
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("distPlot")
    )
  )
))


### server.r
library(lattice)
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  output$distPlot <- renderPlot({
 
    dat <- data.frame(v1 = rnorm(1000), v2 = rnorm(1000), id = gl(5,200))
    xyplot(v1~v2|id, dat, layout = c(1,5))
 
  })
})
